mergedFrom.summary: Notification-planning rule re-implemented in the backend instead of shared with the frontend's `planCommentNotifications` — two implementations that already give different answers

finding.summary: Notification planning + mention parsing reimplemented in the backend instead of shared, so two copies of the same rule now exist
finding.evidence: `planCommentNotifications`, `toUserId` and `MENTION_RE` in comments.controller.ts are line-for-line restatements of `packages/frontend/src/components/comments/notify.ts:29-114` and `mentions.ts`' `MENTION_RE`/`extractMentionedUserIds`. The docblock openly says it "applies the same rule the frontend's notify.ts does", and notifications.md (as amended here) promises "membership authorization, the recipient cap and the dedupe keys stay one implementation" — but the *planning* rule (who is a recipient, mention-vs-reply dedupe, actor exclusion) is now two implementations that must be edited in lockstep. The repo's stated posture is reuse via a shared package (`@wafflebase/core`, and the comment engine itself already lives in `@wafflebase/sheets`, from which this controller imports `createThread`/`addReply`/`deleteComment`), so the planning rule and mention regex had an available shared home. Divergence gives two different answers to "who gets notified for this comment" depending on whether the writer was a browser or an agent.

verdict.reason: The claimed duplication is not present. comments.controller.ts contains no local planCommentNotifications, no toUserId, and no MENTION_RE; it imports planCommentNotifications from @wafflebase/sheets (lines 45-50) and calls that import inside notify() (line 197). The planning rule — recipient selection, mention-vs-reply dedupe (!mentioned.includes(id)), actor exclusion (isActor), and id coercion (toNotifiableUserId) — exists in exactly one place: packages/sheets/src/comment/notify-plan.ts:49-151, exported via packages/sheets/src/index.ts:244-253. The frontend notify.ts is a thin adapter delegating to that same shared function (notify.ts:6 and :37), so both writers execute one implementation and cannot diverge. The mention grammar is single-sourced too: MENTION_RE exists only at packages/sheets/src/comment/mentions.ts:30, and packages/frontend/src/components/comments/mentions.ts:13-21 re-exports the shared parsers unchanged. A repo-wide grep for MENTION_RE/toUserId/extractMentionedUserIds finds no backend copy. The reviewer's quoted docblock is inverted: comments.controller.ts:99-104 says it uses the *same function* the editor calls "rather than a second statement of it", and docs/design/notifications.md:35-39 records that restating the rule in the controller "was tried first and is what the shared module replaces", including the exact preview divergence the finding predicts as a pending risk. The alleged user-facing cost (two different answers to "who gets notified" for browser vs agent writers) is therefore impossible.

mergedFrom.summary: No comment-edit route, although the documented comment lifecycle is edit *and* delete

finding.summary: Comment/thread delete routes enforce no author check, contradicting the documented "delete by author only" lifecycle
finding.evidence: `deleteThread` and `deleteComment` take only `@Param`s — no `@Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest` and no comparison of `req.user.id` against `comment.author.userId` — so any workspace member holding a `write`-scoped key can delete another user's thread or reply. `docs/design/sheets/comments.md:32` states the model as "Comment lifecycle: edit / delete by author only", and the editor enforces exactly that (`packages/frontend/src/components/comments/components/CommentThreadCard.tsx:92`: `c.author.userId === currentUserId`). The new surface therefore permits a destructive action the documented design forbids, and it is irreversible (the thread is removed from the CRDT). Every other comment verb in this controller does resolve the caller (`this.author(req)`), which makes the omission look unintentional rather than a decision recorded anywhere in the diff or in notifications.md.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the delete routes take "only @Params — no @Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest and no comparison of req.user.id against comment.author.userId". The source shows the opposite. deleteThread (comments.controller.ts:439-467) declares @Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest at line 444, resolves `const author = await this.author(req)` at line 447, and passes an authorize callback (lines 460-464) calling `this.assertCommentAuthor(map, threadId, rootCommentId(thread), author)`. deleteComment (comments.controller.ts:469-505) does the same at lines 475, 478 and 502. assertCommentAuthor (comments.controller.ts:519-534) throws ForbiddenException when `commentAuthorId(comment) !== caller.userId`. The check is reachable and runs pre-mutation: mutateMap invokes `authorize?.(...)` before doc.update on both the sheet path (line 562) and the flat doc/pdf path (line 578). The comparison is substantive, not a no-op: commentAuthorId (comment-ops.ts:228-231) returns the stored string author.userId, and findComment (comment-ops.ts:213-218) resolves the target comment. The cited design doc further contradicts the premise: docs/design/sheets/comments.md:31-38 records that comments.controller.ts checks the stored author.userId against the authenticated caller before an edit or delete, and that thread deletion is authorized as deleting its opening comment — exactly what rootCommentId (comments.controller.ts:613-615) implements. No spec divergence exists; the described code is not present.
